item.description:
### Added
- Nodex runs on Windows 11, on both x64 and Arm PCs. Download the installer from nodex.jyu.app: it installs for your account without administrator rights, and Nodex keeps itself up to date from Stable or Nightly as it does on macOS. Choose PowerShell, Command Prompt or Git Bash for new terminals in General settings. - Nodex stays available in the Windows notification area when you close its last window, so chats and scheduled tasks keep running. Open Nodex, start a new chat or return to a recent chat from the tray. Nodex starts quietly at login; manage this in Windows Startup Apps from General settings. - Codex sets up its Windows sandbox once before working in Ask for approval or Approve for me. The notice beside the composer offers Set up, which asks for administrator approval, and setup without it if that doesn't work; Full access needs no setup. - Sites in the built-in Browser can ask for your camera, microphone, location, notifications and other permissions. The request appears under the address bar, where you allow it while visiting, allow it this time or never allow it; Site information lists what each site may do and resets it, and a permission your system blocks offers to open System Settings. - Sort chats by Last updated or Manual order from the options menu in the sidebar's Projects header. Manual order keeps the chats you arrange where you put them, with new and never-arranged chats above them by activity, and switching between the two keeps your arrangement. - A Page's Files read as a file tree, and each File opens in a tab beside its Page. Folders, kinds and sizes sit across the Page's full width, with which chat or person attached each File and when. HTML reports render as the pages they are, with their images and data from the same Page, in an offline preview that cannot reach the network or your files; images, PDFs, Markdown and code open in their own viewers. A report an Agent attaches again updates the open tab. - Agents that Nodex runs are named on the Files they attach through the `nodex` CLI, so each File records the chat it came from. Files attached from your own terminal are recorded as added from the command line, and `nodex page file list` reports who attached each File and when. - Choose what each chat's Agent may do on your computer: Ask for approval, Approve for me, or Full access. Ask for approval keeps the Agent in its workspace and asks before it reaches the network or changes other files. New chats start with Full access; change the default in Settings → Agents and any chat's mode from the composer, with Full access confirmed whenever you turn it on. When the Agent needs permission, the request appears where it stopped with the exact command or change, and you approve it, decline it, or just send a message to redirect the Agent. Delegated tasks never exceed their parent's mode, Agents cannot approve each other, and every Agent keeps full access to your Pages and chats in every mode. - Agents can answer the questions other chats ask. `session_question` reads and answers a pending question in another chat, and the Agent that delegated a task answers its questions with `task_question`, woken by the question or returned from its wait. Each answer shows which conversation gave it, and approvals still come to you. - Agents can stop another chat, mark chats read or unread, and manage the messages queued behind a chat's current turn, within the same permissions as that chat. - Ask a chat to remind you later when something pulls you away. Remind me, in a chat's menu or the command palette, makes it unread again in an hour, in three hours, in the morning or next week, with a notification; replying or archiving cancels it, and Agents can set one with `set_session_reminder`. A clock marks a chat with a pending reminder, and a pencil marks one where you left a reply unsent. `⇧⌘U` marks the current chat unread to come back to it. - New page in the command palette creates a page where you are and opens it beside you: in your Project's database in a Project or one of its chats, and in Space otherwise. - Choose which Claude, Codex and Nodex credit meters appear in the rail from General settings. Hidden meters stop checking usage while account and model access stay available. - Sign in with your Nodex Account to choose GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5 or Claude Sonnet 5.5 using prepaid credit. Buy credit in Account settings through Stripe Checkout; the rail's credit meter shows what is left, and models follow live availability. - Pages can hold Prompts: write a prompt with `/prompt`, then press `⌘↵` or its send button to send it to the chat beside the Page, or to a new chat in the Page's Project. The Prompt stays in the Page and follows its own turn in that chat, from Queued to Answered; open it to read the reply, jump to the message in the chat, or insert the reply into the Page under the Prompt. A Page can keep a series of prompts or one you reuse. - Ask for change rewrites a Page selection with AI and shows you the result before anything changes. Pick it from the selection menu, say what you want or tap Improve writing, Make shorter or Fix spelling & grammar, then Accept, Try again, or ask for another change to the proposal. - Chats can reference Pages beside the Composer, including highlighted Blocks, or mention any Library Page with `@`. Sent references reopen their Page without creating a Linked chat relationship. - An empty Inbox shows how it will plan your next messages: the model that writes suggestions, Nodex's model guide beside what is left of each Agent's weekly budget, and your routing preferences. Change the suggestion model or write your routing preferences right there. - Inbox suggestions know which OpenCode models are free, so routine work such as docs and notes can go to them without spending a plan's budget. - Agent replies recover on their own when the Agent gives up for a transient reason. After a dropped connection, a busy or overloaded model, a request rate limit or an Agent process that stopped mid-reply, the reply shows what happened and when it will retry, then continues where it left off in the same conversation without resending your request. Lost connections keep retrying for as long as you are offline, so work resumes when you reconnect, and a model at capacity keeps retrying for about an hour. Stop, a new message or another model takes over at once, and delegated tasks show Retrying instead of failing their Agent.
### Changed
- Desktop packages take less disk space by sharing one Claude Code runtime and omitting redundant terminal binaries and debug files. - Agent problems no longer appear as red text inside the composer. When the Agent a chat uses is signed out, turned off, missing or not ready, a quiet notice attached to the composer says so and offers the fix, such as Sign in, Check again or Settings, and leaves once it is fixed; a chat that has no usable Agent yet stays quiet while the model picker shows what each Agent needs. A message that does not go out and other failed actions say what failed in a toast, and your draft stays where it was. - Show more and Show less in the sidebar now move five rows at a time. Show less hides only the rows the last Show more revealed, so you can step a list back instead of collapsing it to its first page, and a last remaining row appears with the rest instead of waiting behind its own Show more. This applies to Projects, each Project's chats, Chats, custom Sections and Space Content. - Links now open where you choose. Web links open in your default browser and local development sites in Nodex's Browser unless you change either in Settings → Browser, and local HTML files always open in the Browser. ⌘-click sends a web link to your default browser (change or unassign it in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts), ⌘⇧-click opens it in a new Browser tab, a middle-click opens it in a background tab, and ⌥-click saves it. The same rules apply to links in chats, Pages, terminals, MCP apps and interactive replies, and to files you click in chats. - The built-in Browser opens what a desktop browser opens. Type a file path to view a local file, follow `file:` and `data:` links, and open pages whose links carry a sign-in; a page that opens a new window gets a tab right beside it, and its links offer Open in new tab, Open in new window and Open in external browser. - Files an Agent makes for you now appear as cards under its reply and in the chat summary's Outputs, in Project chats too. Each card names the file with its kind and folder; HTML reports open in Nodex's Browser as the pages they are, other files open in a preview, and Open in lists every app that can open the file, with Show in Finder and Download a copy. Code the Agent edits in your repository stays in Review instead of showing up as an output, while a report it writes to an ignored folder such as `notes.local/` counts. - Backups no longer wait for your Agents. Creating a snapshot from Settings → Backups or with `nodex backup create` works while chats are replying, and never pauses Codex, Claude Code or another Agent, including ones you run outside Nodex. A snapshot holds your Pages, Databases, Library Files and Projects and how your chats are organized; chat transcripts and each Agent's own history are no longer copied into every snapshot, which keeps snapshots small and quick. - Restoring a snapshot rewinds your content, not your chats. Pages, Databases, Files and Projects return to the snapshot, while chats keep their latest messages and continue with their Agents; chats started after the snapshot stay, and chats you deleted stay deleted. Replies that are still running stop before Nodex restarts. - Page stages are now Triage, Plan, Doing, Review and Done, words that fit any kind of work. Build is now Doing and Ship is now Done; your Pages keep their stage, and a stage you renamed keeps your name. Command-line and API callers use `doing` and `done`. Review now means waiting on someone else's verdict; checking an Agent's work round after round stays in Doing, where the Page's chat activity shows whose turn it is. - Handing a Page to a chat moves it to Doing. Open in new chat, Send to chat and sending a Prompt start a Page that is still in Triage or Plan, so you no longer move its card yourself. A Page in Review or Done keeps its stage, and an Agent finishing its work never changes it. - New chats now start at the top of Chats and of their Project, and chats are ordered by when you last wrote in them or a reminder brought them back. Agent replies no longer move a chat, so the list holds still while Agents work, and a chat's hover card shows that same time. Before, a new chat could land at the very bottom of a long list. - Expanding the composer that floats over full-width content now shows the whole chat, not just the latest reply. It opens at the newest message and scrolls on its own without moving your place in the chat, with the same collapsed work, Find and message navigation as the chat itself. - You can now tell at a glance which Agent does another chat's work. A subagent's details, its row in Subagents and its own header mark its Agent beside the model, such as Codex GPT-6.1 Sol under a Claude chat, and its header adds the effort it was given. A message another chat sent, an answer another Agent gave and a fork's origin name that chat with its Agent's mark instead of "another agent", and open it. Subagents that report back read like the row that started them, by name, and each name opens its subagent. - Agents can retry Nodex tool calls safely with any `idempotencyKey` they choose, across turns and restarts. A rejected call now names each invalid argument and why. - Send to chat sends a Page selection to the chat beside the Page in one click or with `⌘⇧↵`, without choosing a chat or a mode; its chevron still opens the chat picker, which lists the Page's linked chats first. Add to composer (`⌥⌘↵`) puts the selection into that chat's draft so you can add a few words before sending. Both shortcuts can be changed in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts. - Waiting on another chat also returns once that chat starts waiting on you for an answer, a secret or an approval, and Agents see a chat's waiting state the same way whichever Agent runs it. - Chats waiting for your answer or approval show an orange question bubble instead of the blue unread dot, so waiting and unread can be told apart at a glance. The same glyph marks waiting chats in collapsed Projects and Sections, chat and side chat tabs, the Project chat picker and a Page's chat activity. - `C` now captures a thought to the Inbox where you are instead of opening the new-page form. You just write; Nodex names the message, or you can name it yourself with Add title. It lands in your Project's Inbox when you are in a Project or one of its chats, and in your main Inbox otherwise, without taking you anywhere. The full-window `V` form is gone; a board's own New page still opens the page form. - `⌘⇧D` in a Project's chat now opens that Project's Inbox, the same Inbox its Agents send to, instead of your main Inbox. - A chat in the sidebar keeps showing the status of the page it started from when more pages are linked to it, instead of showing none. The first linked page that still exists is the one it follows. - New page in a New tab now creates the page in its Project's database instead of Space, where it gets a key and a status and sits with the Project's other pages. A page made from a chat is also linked to that chat, so the page keeps a way back to the chat after its tab closes. Chats without a Project still put new pages in Space. - Images in a chat message now reach the Agent as images, not as text that names them. A Page image you copy and paste into a chat or the Inbox joins the attachment row as the image itself, whether it was copied with its Library reference or as a local path. An image written into the message, or into an edit of it, travels as an image marked where it sits and numbered after the attached ones, and a file on disk keeps its path so the Agent can work with it. A web image stays a link the Agent can open. - A sent message shows the images its text refers to right there, as small images that open in the message's image viewer alongside its attachments. Right-clicking one of a message's images offers the same actions as an image in the Agent's reply, including Add to chat, Copy image and Reveal. - Editing an Inbox message no longer asks for a new suggestion every time you pause. The suggestion stays beside the message, marked as written before it changed, and you can still confirm it or choose Suggest again. Opening, moving or renaming a message's Page leaves its suggestion as it was. - Inbox suggestions take a short look around before proposing where a message goes, instead of judging from its few words alone. The suggestion Agent reads the Project's files, searches the web, and points the chat it suggests at what it found, so that chat starts from the right place on a model that fits the work. Notes and reminders are left as they are, and your routing preferences can tell it when not to look. Suggestions see only what Nodex gives them, never your personal Agent instructions, skills or MCP servers, and their prompts no longer restate your project's agent rules. - Inbox suggestions no longer plan delegated parts of a new chat. A chat suggestion now keeps what you asked for in its prompt and lists what it added on its own beneath it, such as a hint to hand part of the work to another model or a file it found worth reading, each with a checkbox. Uncheck any you don't want sent; the chat's Agent decides how to delegate. - Inbox suggestions read each message whole: its formatting, links and lists as you wrote them, and its images as images. A screenshot with a single line of text is understood for what it shows, and a chat started from the Inbox receives the message the same way. - Images in a message you send to the Inbox now come first on its Page, matching how the stream shows them above the text. - You choose when Inbox suggestions run: automatically for each message you send, only when you ask, or never, from the Inbox's settings gear or Settings → Inbox. Automatic suggestions pause when the suggestion Agent's usage is about to run out and say so above the composer; Suggest still works on any message. - An inline equation in Pages, messages and the Inbox is now written only as `$$…$$`. `\(…\)`, and `\[…\]` within a line, mean the parentheses and brackets themselves, as GitHub reads them. `\[` and `\]` on lines of their own still make an equation Block, and Agent replies in chat still show both spellings as equations. - An Agent woken by a finished delegated task now continues from the task's result right away instead of first asking Nodex for it. Results up to 16 KB in total arrive with the wake; a longer one is still read with `task_status`.
### Removed
- Send & wrap is gone from Send to chat. Sending leaves the Page as it is; use a Prompt when you want the Page to keep what you asked and where it went.
### Fixed
- Nodex opens existing Profiles after an upgrade even when they contain older chat cleanup records or Pages written by an earlier Markdown serializer.
- Codex chats running side by side no longer all stop at once. When one chat's output arrived faster than Nodex could keep up, or Nodex failed to record one of its events, Nodex closed the Codex process the chats share, and every reply ended with "The provider event stream closed unexpectedly". Now only that chat catches up with Codex while the others keep going, and replies whose Codex process does stop resume on their own. - An Agent that delegates tasks now always learns how they ended. A brief local read failure as a task finished could leave it shown as working to the delegating chat until Nodex restarted, so the Agent was never woken; Nodex now retries that handoff and rechecks unsettled tasks every minute. - Changes that finish saving during a brief slowdown are no longer reported as failed. Nodex used to show a timeout or cancellation for a save that had already completed. - Cancelling worktree setup now waits for its commands to stop before removing the worktree. If a command cannot be stopped, Nodex keeps its files and reports the failure. - Agents can use the in-app Browser when you start Nodex from inside another desktop app, such as from its terminal, or when that app shares your Codex settings. Browser actions used to fail with "native pipe path unavailable" because they tried to reach the other app's private services; Nodex now ignores what that app leaves behind and keeps its Browser on its own. - Hovering an Agent's reply now shows when it arrived. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and ACP chats keep each reply's time, and it stays the same after you reopen a chat or restart Nodex. - Automatic snapshots now keep their schedule when you restart Nodex often. The next one is due one interval after your newest snapshot, Nodex takes an overdue one shortly after it starts, and a failed attempt is retried sooner instead of waiting a full interval. - A Claude Code chat whose transcript was removed from Claude's history now continues instead of failing. Like Codex chats, its next message starts a fresh Claude session that receives the chat's earlier messages. - The Changed files list in Files and Review no longer blinks while Git status refreshes. It keeps showing the current list until the refreshed one is ready, including in repositories with untracked files. - A stage you rename in a Database now shows its new name everywhere: Board columns, List groups, filters, Page search, mentions and Move to no longer fall back to the default name. - Agent replies are no longer marked failed when Nodex, not the Agent, has a hiccup. A local read failure could fail several running replies at once with "Provider turn failed." while their Agents kept working and even finished; Nodex now reconnects to the Agent and keeps the real outcome, and failures that start in Nodex say what happened. - A delegated task can no longer stay "working" forever after a failure. Every running reply is checked against its Agent, so a follow-up sent into a task that was still finishing its previous turn completes with that turn instead of hanging, and its delegating Agent is woken when it ends. - Returning to a chat whose side panel shows a large file no longer freezes the window. Files appear at once as plain text and gain syntax colors in the background, a large file becomes editable as soon as its colors arrive, and switching back to it later shows it highlighted and editable right away. Source views of Page Files open the same way. - Large diffs in Review and in chat no longer freeze the window. They appear at once and gain syntax colors in the background, and returning to a chat shows them highlighted right away. - Show changes on a very large or heavily edited file no longer freezes the window. The file stays open and editable with a note that the comparison is too large to show, instead of a retry that could never succeed. Comparing your unsaved edits with a version changed on disk works the same way. - Searching chats from the command palette now finds every chat by its title, including chats beyond your most recent hundred, Claude, OpenCode and Agent Runtime chats, and any part of a Chinese or Japanese title. A typo or a branch, Project or pull request name finds a chat too. The same search powers chat mentions, Send to chat and adding a chat to the composer. Message history is searched once you pause typing; a slow or unavailable history no longer hides title matches, and the palette says when some history couldn't be searched. - Editing a sent message in an Agent chat now replaces only that message and what came after it, never earlier messages. Messages that can't be edited that way no longer show Edit. - Long chats can recover from context exhaustion with Compact and retry while keeping their history and original request. Delegated results already received by the Agent are no longer sent again after a failed reply. - Opening a side chat's notification now returns to the chat you opened it from, with the side chat selected in its panel, instead of showing the side chat alone. Replying from the notification goes to the side chat. - Replying to an Agent chat from its notification now sends your reply. Before, it opened the chat and dropped what you wrote. - Starting a side chat with `/side` and a message no longer leaves that message in the side chat's message box, where pressing Enter would send it a second time. - A chat no longer stays marked as waiting after one of its delegated tasks asked a question and finished. A chat now waits only on what needs you: its own questions once the Agent stops working, approvals, and its side chats' questions. A question left at the end of a turn sends one question notification rather than a completion too, and a finished task's unanswered question no longer keeps Nodex's Agent process running. - Collapsed Projects and Sections now show when any of their chats is waiting or working, including Agent chats the sidebar has not loaded, and a chat asking for approval or input shows as waiting instead of working. - Sending from a Page to a chat that the sidebar has not loaded yet no longer fails with "This chat is no longer available". - Add to chat in the Files tree now puts the file into the chat's composer every time, instead of sometimes appearing to do nothing until the chat redrew. - Opening a Page with images no longer saves an unintended edit when its images load. - Backspace while composing text with an input method, such as Chinese Pinyin, no longer cuts off what you're typing in a Page. The input method keeps your text, so its letters no longer end up in the Page. - Images in chat messages that point to a file or to a Page's image now show instead of appearing broken. A file path, such as a Page image copied as a local path, shows that file, read from the chat's host when the chat runs on another machine, and an image copied with its Library reference shows too. Pages show images written as file paths the same way. - Sending a Page that shows web images, such as status badges, to a chat no longer fails. - Relative image paths in chat messages and Agent replies now show, read from the chat's working folder. - An image written as `![caption](path)` in a chat message is no longer mistaken for a file mention. - A `file://` link that names a network share opens that share instead of a local path with the same name. - A queued message in a chat on another machine no longer reads its image paths from this computer. - Copying from a Page no longer puts a backslash before periods, commas, question marks and `&`. A parenthesis or bracket in a paragraph used to leave most punctuation after it escaped, both in what you pasted into a chat or another app and in the text Agents read and edit. Now a backslash appears only where the character would otherwise become formatting, existing Pages are rewritten when Nodex updates, and web addresses copy without one, so they still open wherever you paste them. - Web and mail addresses in plain text pasted into a Page now become links, while each line keeps exactly its text. - Notes Nodex sends to wake an Agent no longer show up among your queued messages. When a delegated task finished while Claude was mid-reply, its "Delegated task … reached a terminal state" note sat in your queue, where Steer failed and Delete quietly cancelled the wake-ups for the rest of that turn's tasks. The queue now holds only what you and other chats sent; the Agent still continues on its own, and the chat shows which task finished. - Clicking a tab's close button right after the tab opens now always closes it. The tabs used to shift under the pointer as the press began, so the release could land beside the button and the click did nothing. - A subagent you already loaded in the Subagents overview no longer disappears when its status changes. A row that sorted past the loaded part of the list after an update used to vanish until you loaded more.
### Security
- While an Agent controls a Browser tab, it can take that tab only to web pages: redirects, embedded frames and pop-ups are checked the whole time it is in control, and the tab is yours again as soon as the Agent lets go.
